description.narrative:
Sida jointly with the EU, under a delegated support, contributes to the strengthening of the capacity of the National Institute of Statistics (NIS) in Cambodia through the "Cooperation Project between the National Institute of Statistics in Cambodia and Statistics Sweden" in Cambodia during the period 2020-2022.
The intervention aims at improving the quality of statistical production in Cambodia as well as the utilization of statistics by 1) improving the quality and utilization of National Accounts; 2) improve the statistical capacity within NIS as well as the National Statistical System; 3) ensure a stable ICT infrastructure and ICT systems for managing, producing and disseminating data and Statistics; 4) improve the dissemination of key Statistics in a user-friendly way; and 5) strengthen internal coordination within NIS as well as the wider coordination mechanisms for coordination within the National Statistical System.
The project is part of the second phase of the Sida/EU financed PAT Programme (Partnership for Accountability and Transparency, PAT II, GD decision 2019-003682) contributing to its overall goal "Strengthened demand for and supply of public transparency and accountability through institutional capacity development".
The intervention’s total budget financed by Sida/EU is SEK 15 600 000.

Sida tillsammans med EU (genom delegering till Sida) finansierar ett kapacitetsstöd till den kambodjanska statistikbyrån, National Institute of Statistics, (NIS), för att med hjälp av svenska statistiska centralbyrån SCB, genomföra "Cooperation Project between the National Institute of Statistics in Cambodia and Statistics Sweden" i Kambodja under perioden 2020-2022.
Insatsen syftar till att förbättra kvaliteten på statistisk produktion i Kambodja såväl som användningen av denna statistik genom att 1) ??förbättra kvaliteten och användningen av national räkenskaperna. 2) förbättra den statistiska kapaciteten inom NIS såväl som det nationella statistiska systemet; 3) säkerställa en stabil ICT-infrastruktur och ICT-system för att hantera, producera och sprida data och statistik; 4) göra presentationen av statistik mer användarvänlig och; 5) stärka samordningen inom NIS och inom nationella statistiska systemet.
Insatsen är en del av den andra fasen av en större finansiering från Sida/EU (Partnership for Accountability and Transparency, PAT II, GD-beslut 2019-003682) som har som delmål att stärka efterfrågan på och tillgången till ansvarsutkrävande i den offentliga sektorn genom institutionell kapacitetsutveckling.
Insatsens totala budget finansierad av Sida/EU är SEK 15 600 000.

The intervention forms one part of the Partnership for Accountability and Transparency (PAT) II programme. The PAT programme aims to complement EU's sector budget support to the PFM reform with the objective to facilitate "an enabling environment for the PFM reform by strengthened demand for and supply of public transparency and accountability through institutional capacity development". The overall objective for the intervention in the area of statistics is “that reliable and transparent statistical information is available for use in decision-making and for accountability”. NIS and Statistics Sweden will collaborate in four different areas. The expected outcomes per component are: Component 1: National Accounts - Improved quality and usage of National Accounts. - New socioeconomic data available for use in national accounts and other analysis (including SDGs). Component 2: Statistical methods - Statistical capacity improved within NIS and the national statistical system. Component 3: Communication and ICT - NIS has a stable ICT infrastructure and ICT systems for managing data, producing data and disseminating statistics. - NIS is able to disseminate key statistics in a user-friendly way. Increased statistical literacy among key users. Component 4: Management and Organisational Structure - Strengthened internal coordination within NIS. - Strengthened mechanisms for coordination within the national statistical system.

The overall project objective was to ensure that objective and transparent statistical information is available for use in implementing the public finance management reforms in Cambodia.The project focused on specific components. These components were national account, statistical methods, communication and ICT and management and organization structure. The institutional cooperation was implemented during January 1, 2020 December 31, 2022.
Main achievements/results:
National Accounts
The specific outcomes were:
- Improved quality and usage of National Accounts
- New socioeconomic data available for use in national accounts and other analyses (i.e. SDGs)
The main outputs:
Time series with new base year 2014 have been recalculated, from old 2014 time series to new 2021 time series and back casting to 2000. NIS have developed a roadmap to improve Macroeconomic Statistics. The roadmap includes NIS, MEF and National Bank of Cambodia (NBC) and the aim is to improve the quality in Government Financial Statistics, Balance of Payment and National Accounts. The roadmap receives funding from the government in term of funding, but also from IMF in regards of capacity building. The roadmap was approved and commenced during 2022. A simplified calculation system, as well as training material and documentation, have been developed. Also, a strategy for improved quality and communication of the National Accounts have been developed. National Accounts are now using taxation data from GDT, however not regularly (a decision is needed from top government level for each data sharing).
The results achieved: For National Accounts the work has been focused on compiling GDP and its components for the years 2015-2018, to align the time series to the benchmark estimates for 2014. As a part of this work methods and sources used for the compilation have been evaluated. NIS has also continued the discussions with General Department of Taxation (GDT) to be able to use taxation data for the GDP. Taxation data has been used during 2022, but in an informal way. This means that there is no formalized MoU between NIS and GDT. However, a decision was taken during 2022 by Deputy Prime Minister of Cambodia that GDT needs to share data with NIS for the compilation of NA and GDP during a certain time frame. For the future the sharing process will need to be formalized on top government level. It has not possible to agree on an institutional level during PAT II. However, NIS are now able to maintain, change and update the GDP calculation system. A peer review of the GDP with the new time series was done in August 2022, with consultants from Statistics Sweden and IMF. The quality was assessed to be good. The new GDP will be published early 2023.
Statistical Methods
The specific outcome was:
- Statistical capacity improved within NIS and the national statistical system
The main outputs:
NIS has a Methodology Team with members from different departments. Documentation regarding roles and responsibilities within the Methodology Team have been developed. NIS can conduct courses in basic statistics (Statistics in Action, STAC), without support from Statistics Sweden. NIS is using their own teachers, using Khmer language and training material in Khmer. NIS can design statistical surveys.
Results achieved: Three more courses in basic statistics (STAC) were conducted during 2022. One STAC course was held in Mondul Kiri province in January, one STAC course in Kampot province in May and one STAC course in Battambang province in September. During 2022 staff from line ministries participated in the STAC courses. The STAC courses were conducted with teachers from NIS and in Khmer language. A two-week mission was conducted by Statistics Sweden in November 2022 where methodology documentation was reviewed and assessed to have good quality.
Communication and ICT
The specific outcomes were:
- NIS has a stable ICT infrastructure and ICT system for managing data and disseminating statistics
- NIS is able to disseminate key statistics in a user-friendly way
- Increased statistical literacy among key users
The main outputs:
NIS have a Publishing Team with members from different departments. NIS have increased knowledge in network administration, server administration, administration of the virtualized environment and security administration. An ICT strategy, with corresponding policies was developed during the project (the strategy and policies still needs to be formally implemented). A publishing process, as well as a dissemination policy have been developed.
Results achieved: During 2022 there have been hands on training, on a daily basis, in the areas of ICT infrastructure administration of the ICT Department. Also, work has continued with the draft ICT strategy as well as developing ICT policies. Four more courses were conducted during 2022. Two courses in databases and two courses in Excel, with a total of 99 participants, 25 women and 74 men. The courses have been targeting all staff at NIS working with statistical production.
During 2022 three short missions were also conducted, with focus on dissemination of statistics through the NIS website. The missions also included subjects like how to write press releases in plain language and for specific target groups.
Management and Organization Structure
The specific outcomes were:
- Strengthened internal coordination within NIS
- Strengthened mechanisms for coordination within the national statistical system
The main outputs:
A tool for a detailed workplan and budgeting of statistical activities have been developed. NIS have increased knowledge in planning and budgeting. Support to the Women Network at NIS.
Results achieved: The work within management and organization structure has been focusing on planning and budgeting at NIS. This work is based on the needs stated in the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics 2019-2023 (NSDS). Three short-term missions have been conducted during 2022. The work during the missions focused on work with the budget framework and planning tool that was developed during 2021. In addition, a two-day workshop was held in April 2022, in Sihanoukville, for the Women Network with the objective to providing training on gender issues and to find gender related indicators in the 2019 census data using the Redatam software. Another two-day workshop for the Women Network was held in December 2022, in Siem Reap, as a continuation of the previous workshop with more advanced training in the Redatam software.
Other satisfactory achievements
Gender
The project has been working to promote a gender balance within NIS by supporting the Women Network. The network, led by the Director General of NIS, is providing a forum for women in management positions in NIS to discuss relevant issues, gain skills and work towards a more equal gender balance within the organization as well as developing capacity among the staff about gender issues related to statistics. A two-day workshop was held in April 2022, in Sihanoukville, for the Women Network with the objective to providing training on gender issues and to find gender related indicators in the 2019 census data using the Redatam software. Another two-day workshop for the Women Network was held in December 2022, in Siem Reap, this workshop was a continuation of the previous workshop with more advanced training in the Redatam software. The project has encouraged a gender balance in all activities where possible and has after discussions with top management promoted the inclusion of women in the publishing and methodology teams, which NIS has done. The gender balance in the publishing team is 30 percent women and 70 percent men. For the methodology team the gender balance is 25 percent women and 75 percent men.
With Swedish development cooperation, NIS has improved its monitoring of gender equality statistics. In 2020, NIS conducted a gender in statistics assessment. NIS used PARIS21s and UN Womens Framework and Implementation Guidelines for assessing gender statistics, as the tool for the assessment. NIS also evaluated gender data gaps and relevant statistical capacities, both within NIS and across the NSS. NIS also assessed data and statistical capacity gaps for better gender statistics and analyzed the state of gender statistics to strengthen the national capacity to produce, use and monitor better quality gender statistics, including the gender relevant indicators of SDGs. According to the World Economic Forums Global Gender Gap Index, Cambodia has marginally increased its overall gender equality (from 0.629 in 2006 to 0.685 in 2021, a score of one representing gender equality). However, the recent gender statistics assessment finds that the capacity of the technical staff from NIS and Ministry of Womens Affairs, in computing and analyzing gender statistics is still limited and additional training is needed. To address this challenge, the World Bank is supporting to update gender statistics, by using the most recent available census data. Some key indicators, such as education, employment, disability and housing amenities, can be directly generated from the 2019 Population and Housing Census, as well as entrepreneurship indicators from the 2022 Economic Census. These indicators will be representative at sub-national level i.e., province, district and commune. During PAT I the project supported the 2019 Population and Housing Census.
Sustainability
NISs ownership has gradually grown stronger throughout the project period. At the end, it could be considered quite strong. The work with the project cooperation has primarily been improved by dedicated project teams, that was established to work closely together with the Long-Term Advisor (LTA) managing all project activities. An increased use of digital platforms has improved the cooperation in the organization, not at least during the pandemic, as well as added efficiency to the statistical production.
The project has also focused on sustainability during the last phase as a part of an exit strategy. Training plans and training modules have been produced to mitigate the effects of staff turnover and to develop institutional capacity. All work within the components was done with working teams, with members for different departments (where applicable), in order distribute knowledge to several staff and to avoid a situation with individual key persons at NIS. In this way, NIS has also taken steps into becoming a learning organization.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
